How does Bitcoin work, and can I get rich by mining?

This is one of those things it's easy to get rabbit-holed on. I'm going to try for a very simplified explanation, skipping the cryptography bits.

Essentially Bitcoin is just a way of placing value on computation. To mine a Bitcoin your computer must solve a complex calculation. As more Bitcoins are generated, the complexity of the calculation goes up.

Bitcoin is also a method of transferring this value. One of the big perks of Bitcoin is that it's decentralized - no one entity controls it. When you send Bitcoin to someone the transaction is recorded in the block chain. Think of it as a public ledger of transactions. This is all done in a rather complicated but hopefully secure manner.

No, you probably can't get rich by mining. As the mining complexity goes up it becomes harder and harder to mine. At this point companies are custom-fabricating special purpose mining processors and setting up large farms of them to run in parallel.

I read this theory somewhere online, liked it, and thought it would be appropriate to post here. I'm not taking credit for coming up with it, and don't necessarily agree with it. It's similar to the Ship of Theseus thought experiment, but it's implications might be more profound.

Individualized consciousness is an illusion. Consciousness is just a singular property of existence that emerges when there exists a brain that has evolved to a sufficient level of complexity.

To illustrate, suppose we had a device that could build and rebuild a person one molecule at a time. We take a person and replace all of the molecules in their body while they are conscious. At each stage, it seems reasonable to assume that the person is consciously aware of themselves throughout. Is this the same person as before? I would think so. Now, take all of the original molecules and rebuild that person exactly as they were before.

If this happened to you, what would your experience be? Are you the original or the copy? If consciousness is individualized, we can't make much sense of this. However, if consciousness were just a single property of existence, we can say that they are both you and individuality is an illusion.

Thoughts?

It does resolve the issue neatly to define consciousness this way. I wonder though, how do our illusions of self come to be seemingly different than others? Is there another property or effect that added to this singular consciousness creates what looks like an individual? Is it necessarily imperceptible?
